Tool output safety: upstream generation can truncate large tool arguments even when a high max_tokens was requested. Keep file writes, edits, patches, and generated shell scripts in small complete calls, below 50 lines and 12000 characters of generated content per call. For large files, create a skeleton then fill it in incrementally using the available tools; do not move an oversized payload into a shell heredoc or encoded command. Always include required arguments and close the JSON object. If a tool fails or output is truncated, inspect the current state, reduce the chunk size, and do not repeat the same failed call unchanged. Finish all chunks and verify the final file. Aim to finish this entire response within 4096 output tokens, including reasoning and ALL tool arguments combined. Reserve room to close every JSON object. When a task needs more, return one small complete tool call and continue on the next client turn after its result; do not batch many chunks into one response.
